findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The following food contact surfaces were observed with the accumulation of soil buildup. 
1. The baffles of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of pink mold.
2. The internal surface of the tea and coffee makers were observed to have a buildup of soil.

Discussed with PIC. All food contact surfaces mentioned were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) The following facility maintenance issues were observed.
1. The tile trim in the utility closet was observed coming off the wall. 
2. (REPEAT ) An accumulation of grease and food debris were observed under the fryers and grill in the kitchen. 
 PIC was made aware. Ensure that the accumulation is cleaned and trim sealed properly providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

 Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Multiple wet mop heads were observed stored on the floor on the utility closet including in the draining pit. Discussed with PIC. PIC instructed a staff member to remove the mop heads and have them stored properly. Ensure that proper mop storage procedures are followed at all times.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(E) The chlorine concentration in the dish machine tested at zero. Multiple testing attempts were conducted and the concentration appeared lower than the appropriate level. PIC was made aware. Facility is going to use the triple sink until the dish machine is fixed. Ensure that the dish machine is fixed and the sanitizer monitored at a regular frequency. 

Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The following food contact surfaces were observed with the accumulation of soil buildup. 
1. The baffles of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of pink and black molds.
2. The nozzle of the soda machine in the lobby was observed to be soiled. The nozzle was cleaned and sanitized.
3. The internal surface of other tea and coffee makers were observed to have a buildup of soil. The surfaces were cleaned and sanitized. 

Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the surfaces mentioned will be cleaned and sanitized. Inspector will return on 2/9/2026 to follow up on observation 1. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hot holding units in the back of the cook line and part of the one on the cook line to not be holding temperature within the appropriate temperature range. PIC mention that the unit in question sometimes malfunction with temperature holding. They will work on getting an upgrade to a more functional unit. Ensure that these units is repair and calibrated to constantly hold the appropriate temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) The jug of milk in the chest cooler that holds the ice cream condiments was observed to not be date marked properly. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that the milk was opened the previous day. PIC instructed a staff member to properly date mark the milk jug. The jug was dated immediately. Ensure that all food items not used be properly date marked if it is going to be stored for more that 24 hour after opening. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) The following facility maintenance issues were observed.
1. The caulking on the left side of the three compartment sink and the handwashing sink at the front of the cook line were observed in disrepair.
2. Broken tiles in the back area by the dish machine, the front of the grill, and the under the fryers.
3. An accumulation of grease and food debris were observed under the fryers and grill in the kitchen. 
 PIC was made aware. Ensure that the hand sink and the three compartment sink are caulked properly providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

 Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff barehandling ready to eat food items during food prep. Discussed with PIC and an education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are aware to don gloves after handwashing before prepping ready to eat food at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed to the sani bucket on the cook line by the grill measuring low concentration at 0 ppm. Discussed with PIC and the sani bucket was remade. The new solution tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that the sani buckets are monitored and tested at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.

They will work on getting an upgrade to a more function unit. Ensure that this unit is repair and calibrated to constantly hold the appropriate temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil and food debris within the gasket of the stainless steel four compartment cooler on the cook line opposite the fryers. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the gasket of the cooler would be cleaned. Ensure that non food-contract surfaces such as the gasket of the cooler rare cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface to prevent future malfunction to the equipment.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed soiled mop water being stored in a mop bucket and a wet mop head stored on the floor of the utility closet. Discussed with PIC. PIC drained mop bucket in the mop sink and the wet mop head was stored properly. Ensure mop water is disposed of properly after each use.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed raw Reuben meat being stored over fruits and vegetables. Discussed with PIC. PIC moved the raw meat to a different shelf that is an acceptable storage area. Ensure raw meat is never stored above ready to eat foods and that proper storage order is maintained.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket located near the drive thru was tested and recorded at less than 100ppm. This bucket was removed from service and refilled at the dispenser which tested at 200ppm QUAT. Ensure sanitizer buckets are tested and changed out at a freqeuncy necessary to maintain the sanitizer’s efficacy. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following locations were observed to have an accumulation of food soil/debris:
-The gasket of the lettuce prep station drawer cooler.
-The gaskets of the freezer behind the fryer station. 
-The inside of the microwaves along the cook-line.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned to remove the current accumulation of food soil/debris and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop was observed to be stored directly in the basin of the mop sink. The mop was removed from this location and placed into the top portion of the mop bucket to allow it to properly air dry. Ensure mops are stored in a manner that allows for air drying between use.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
